query: Why did Riot nerf Thresh in patch 26.22, and what was changed?
answer: Despite a previous nerf, Thresh remained at the very top of the support pecking order for top-tier players, so Riot nerfed him again in 26.22: base Attack Damage went from 56 to 54, and R (The Box) damage from 250 / 400 / 550 (+100% AP) to 200 / 350 / 500 (+100% AP).

query: What changed for Mel in patch 26.22?
answer: Mel received a midscope update in 26.22 that moves power from early game to scaling. Base stats changed (e.g. Health 640 + 99/level → 590 + 107/level). Her passive's bonus damage per bolt at low levels was lowered (8 → 4 minimum). Q (Radiant Volley) first-hit damage was cut to 60 (+25% AP) while multi-hit damage rose, and it now refunds cooldown when it hits a champion. W (Rebuttal) was reworked into a nova that destroys enemy projectiles and shields, grants move speed and retaliates against destroyed missiles. E (Solar Snare) root duration now scales with distance. R (Golden Eclipse) cooldown went from 120 / 100 / 80 to 120 / 90 / 60 seconds.

query: What did patch 26.22 change about Doran's Bow, and why?
answer: Doran's Bow's Attack Damage was reduced from 8 to 7 in patch 26.22. Riot considered it slightly but clearly too strong: marksmen expected to lean towards Doran's Blade were almost exclusively buying Doran's Bow.

query: What limit on replay downloads was introduced in patch 26.21, and why?
answer: Starting in patch 26.21, replay downloads are limited to 10 per hour. Players can still download their own replays and those of friends and other players. The limit prevents large-scale abuse by bad actors using apps to scrape thousands of replays; a time-based limit was chosen so creators can still make content.

query: When does TFT move to its own standalone client, and what happens to TFT cosmetics in League?
answer: TFT moves to its own standalone client starting November 4th, 2026. Existing TFT cosmetics remain usable in League; the first TFT-only Little Legends arrive on December 1st, and December 15th marks the full separation of TFT cosmetics, including emotes and icons.
